- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or rebound.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75.0), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 2–5% below peak unless sentiment shifts.  
- Model consistently underestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or declining; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment < 0.67.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.00 or negative values), model tends to underestimate; apply upward bias of 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- Model often fails to capture sentiment-driven mean reversion in 10–15 day horizon; if sentiment shifts from positive to negative, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
